title: Who chose the rulers?
hook: Does appointing a ruler establish control of the city?

knows: Selected accounts can describe distinct institutions and dated changes.
doesNotKnow: Moroccan dynasties versus Ottoman regency institutions, avoiding an empire-only binary

objective: Moroccan dynasties versus Ottoman regency institutions, avoiding an empire-only binary

recall.question: Why does an appointed pasha not prove secure city power?
options: Local military power could expel an appointed pasha, as in 1659.
An appointment guaranteed uninterrupted control of the city.
recall.why: The Algiers account describes Halil Aga expelling Ali Pasha and separate local selection, unlike Fez’s royal council and contested dynastic reach.

care: No timeless national binary, popular assent or appointment as proof of uniform control.
